chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad said:

I said to Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, as we had prepared about thirty questions to send to Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him): 'Include this question for me, and do not make it lengthy for him; ask him about the individual Umrah: is the circumambulation of the women obligatory on their owner?' He said, the answer came back for all the questions except this one. So I said to him, 'Send it back in other questions.' The answer came back for all of them except my question. So I said to Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, 'There is something here; single out this question with my name, for you know my status regarding your needs.' So he wrote it to him, and the answer came back: 'Yes, it is obligatory, there is no need [to doubt it].' Then Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid met Isma'il ibn Humayd al-Azraq, with him was the question and the answer, and he said, 'Indeed, Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad has opened up for you a breakthrough, and this is his question and the answer to it.' So Isma'il ibn Humayd entered upon him and asked him about it, and he said, 'Yes, it is obligatory.' Then Isma'il ibn Humayd met Bashir ibn Isma'il ibn 'Ammar al-Sayfani, informed him, so he entered and asked him about it, and he said, 'Yes, it is obligatory.'

key_terms.الْعُمْرَةِ الْمُفْرَدَةِ: Individual Umrah (Umrah performed separately from Hajj)
key_terms.طَوَافُ النِّسَاءِ: Circumambulation of the women (a specific ritual or reference to women's circumambulation)

ai.seo_question: Is the individual Umrah (Umrah al-Mufradah) obligatory according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the jurisprudential significance of 'Umrah al-Mufradah' (Umrah performed independently of Hajj) through a narrative where Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) specifically singled out this question to emphasize its obligatory status ('wajib'). The repeated verification by subsequent scholars confirms that the circumambulation (Tawaf) associated with this individual Umrah is a mandatory requirement, distinguishing it from mere recommendation. This incident underscores the Imam's role in clarifying ritual obligations during the period of the Minor Occultation's precursor era.
